## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the render scatter into the per-particle step eliminates intermediate buffers and can approach the streaming ceiling despite the scatter reduction being non-Halide-expressible.

## Cache saturation
All measured N exceed the L1d spill at N≈963. At q=0.01, cost falls from 11.898 ns/p (N=4000) to 7.845 (N=16000) — overhead amortization — then stays flat at 7.6–7.7 through N=4000000. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces no knee: N=65000 reads 7.676, N=4000000 reads 7.659. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: ~7.6 (q=0.01), ~8.1 (q=0.05), ~10.3 (q=0.25) ns/p in the flat region. No N-dependent cost past N=16000 at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.93 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 35.4% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.25 it falls to 6.61 GB/s (26.2%). The algo is overhead-bound: bandwidth is flat across N past 16000 (8.86–8.93 at q=0.01), with no DRAM transition. Death rate is the only lever, dropping bandwidth from 8.93 to 6.58 GB/s as q rises, reflecting branchy respawn cost. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling.

## Assembly
Vectorization is across components of one particle, not across particles: `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` operate on four floats packed via `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc`. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads one scalar into a vector lane. The scatter dominates: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` implement byte-granular framebuffer writes, each pixel needing load-add-clamp-store for R, G, B. These uncoalesced byte stores cap bandwidth at 35% of ceiling. The 18 `b` and `bl _spawn` reflect the respawn path whose cost rises with death rate.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter never exceeds 35% of ceiling (8.93/25.22 GB/s at q=0.01) because byte-granular framebuffer writes (19 `strb`, 12 `ldrb`) cannot stream, and flat ns/p across N (7.6 at q=0.01 from N=65000 to N=4000000) confirms overhead-bound behavior. Death rate raises the floor from 7.6 to 10.3 ns/p via branchy respawn, but the scatter bottleneck persists at every churn level.
